name: Lions Services, Inc.
also_known_as: Charlotte Workshop for the Blind (historical name, founded 1935)
one_line: Jobs, job training, assistive-technology training, and health programs for people who are blind or visually impaired in Charlotte.

service_area.note: Materials say "Mecklenburg County and surrounding counties," including veterans. Out-of-area referral policy not published — needs verification.

services.label: Jobs and job training (manufacturing)
services.plain_language: Paid work and training in manufacturing for people who are blind or visually impaired.
services.notes: Lions Services is an AbilityOne / National Industries for the Blind manufacturing contractor for the Department of Defense.

services.label: Assistive-technology training (LionsDENN / V360 TECH)
services.plain_language: Hands-on help learning to use an iPhone, a computer, magnifiers, and screen-reader software like JAWS and ZoomText.
services.notes: Confirmed open to the community, not employees only: the intake form is titled the V360 TECH Community Interest Form. See the LionsDENN program record.

services.label: Help getting connected to broadband/internet
services.plain_language: Help getting internet service at home.
services.notes: Delivered through LionsDENN. The LionsDENN page lists broadband connectivity assessment as one of four core service areas.

services.label: Adaptive health-monitoring station and mental-health counseling (LionsHEART)
services.plain_language: A talking glucometer, blood pressure machine, scale, and telehealth access, plus counseling with a professional counselor.
services.notes: The LionsHEART page describes it as serving Lions Services employees and does not state community eligibility. See the LionsHEART program record.

services.label: Small grants for adaptive tools/tech (ROAR Fund)
services.plain_language: Up to $250 a year to buy things like magnifiers, white canes, or smart glasses.
services.notes: The LionsROAR page states "eligible employees up to $250 annually." See the LionsROAR program record.

services.label: Charlotte Braille Trail
services.plain_language: A public outdoor trail with braille and art.
services.notes: Described on lionsservices.org as "a public art and accessibility initiative promoting braille literacy in the community."

services.label: Blind Support Fund to buy adaptive devices
services.plain_language: Help getting devices such as handheld magnifiers, magnification glasses, and talking watches.
services.notes: Named only on lionsservices.org/about/lions-pride/, which says Lions Services "steps in by aiding the acquisition of assistive devices through the Blind Support Fund." No page cross-references it to the ROAR Fund, and no separate application route is published. Whether it is the same money as the ROAR Fund is an open question.

services.label: Eye care assistance for those in financial need
services.plain_language: Help paying for eye care if you cannot afford it.
services.notes: Not documented anywhere on lionsservices.org as of 2026-09-03. It appears only in third-party directory profiles quoting an older mission statement. The current published mission is "Empowering people who are blind to achieve personal and economic independence — since 1935." Do not route anyone here for eye-care funding until confirmed.

Employment application packet (for jobs)

name: Metrolina Association for the Blind
also_known_as: Metrolina Association for the Blind, Inc.
Mecklenburg County Association for the Blind (former name, renamed 1977)
one_line: Low-vision eye exams, daily-living and safe-travel training, assistive tech, counseling, and transportation in Charlotte.

service_area.note: Confirmed verbatim on MAB's own About page (2026-09-03): "The main service areas are Mecklenburg, Cabarrus and Union counties in NC, however any person who is visually impaired may participate in an agency-based service." MAB's Transportation page independently confirms all three counties for rides, correcting third-party listings that described transportation as Mecklenburg-only. The "37 other counties in North and South Carolina" figure appears only in third-party material and is not on mabnc.org. Partner confirmed the primary service region is Charlotte, NC on September 10, 2026.

services.label: Low-vision eye exams and device matching
services.plain_language: An exam that figures out which magnifiers, telescopes, or electronic magnifiers will help you see better.
services.notes: Optometrists Dr. Laurie Hoffman and Dr. Brittany Flaherty. See the MAB Low Vision Clinic record.

services.label: Low-vision therapy
services.plain_language: Practice using your remaining sight and your devices as well as possible.
services.notes: Certified Low Vision Therapist.

services.label: Daily-living skills training
services.plain_language: Learning how to cook, manage money, and run your home with the sight you have.
services.notes: Delivered by Certified Vision Rehabilitation Therapists. MAB's Rehabilitation page lists adaptive kitchen skills, money management, home management, personal communication, clothing management, cleaning, medication management, lighting, and accessing community resources.

services.label: Mini Center (8-week group program)
services.plain_language: An eight-week group program for people who are new to vision loss or whose sight has recently got much worse.
services.notes: Instructional services are not fee based (partner confirmed September 10, 2026). Covers adaptive kitchen skills, signing your name, pouring, money management, orientation and mobility, transportation, labeling, clothing management, home management, descriptive video, assistive technology, and personal communication.

services.label: White-cane / safe-travel training
services.plain_language: Learning to get around safely on your own, including using a white cane.
services.notes: Orientation & Mobility Specialists train clients in sidewalk travel, street crossings, using businesses, and public transportation.

services.label: Assistive-technology training
services.plain_language: Learning screen readers, magnification, iPhone/iPad, and smart speakers.
services.notes: Two Assistive Technology Demonstration Center visits per year were previously listed as free. Instructional services are not fee based (partner confirmed September 10, 2026).

services.label: Case management / social work
services.plain_language: A case manager who does intake, figures out what you need, and helps with counseling, advocacy, and referrals.
services.notes: Each client is assigned a case manager based on the client's ZIP code. Case Management Supervisor Dolly Baxter, 704-887-5131.

services.label: Support groups and counseling
services.plain_language: Talking with others going through vision loss, and with a counselor.
services.notes: Group names and schedule are not published — verification call required.

services.label: Door-through-door transportation
services.plain_language: Rides for people who are blind or visually impaired, with help from your door to the destination's door.
services.notes: Limited availability in the Charlotte region (partner confirmed September 10, 2026). MAB's Transportation page states the service covers Mecklenburg, Union, and Cabarrus counties, Monday to Friday 6:30am to 8:30pm with limited weekend availability. $10 per round trip up to 26 miles; reduced to $5 up to 26 miles for someone living below 125% of poverty. Book at 704-887-5121 or ajimenez@mabnc.org. Confirm current ride availability and fares when booking.

services.label: Accessible document production (ADS)
services.plain_language: Braille, large print, audio, and accessible PDF documents.
services.notes: A business line, not a direct consumer intake path. See the MAB Accessible Document Services record.

services.label: Social events
services.plain_language: Meet others experiencing vision loss at MAB social events.

services.label: Community outreach and vision-loss awareness training
services.plain_language: Learn about vision loss and available community resources.

services.label: Workforce & Academic Readiness instruction
services.plain_language: Instruction for high school students preparing for work and academics.
services.notes: Contact MAB for enrollment details and schedules.

services.label: In-person and group instruction
services.plain_language: MAB provides instruction in person and in groups.
services.notes: Ask which format is offered for your chosen service.

who_qualifies: Anyone experiencing vision loss or blindness; MAB describes serving ages 4–104, not a strict age cutoff.
No income requirement to qualify. Sliding-scale and hardship pricing depend on income.
Primarily the Charlotte, NC region; existing agency-based services may accept people from outside the primary counties.
documentation_required: A current eye report less than one year old for low-vision exams
Insurance information if applicable; co-pays and fees are due at the exam
Hardship application for financial assistance through the case manager; previously required annual renewal
cost: Low-vision and clinical services are insurance billed; co-pays and fees are due at the exam based on insurance or lack of insurance. Instructional services are not fee based. Sliding-scale and hardship pricing are available depending on income. Prescribed devices and Braille supplies may cost extra. Previously published transportation fares: $10 round trip up to 26 miles, or $5 below 125% of poverty; confirm current fares when booking. Hardship applications are arranged through a case manager and previously required annual renewal.
typical_wait: Typically 2–3 months for low-vision exams; wait times for other services vary.

name: Low Vision Rehab Solutions
one_line: In-home low-vision occupational therapy across NC plus telehealth; a sister nonprofit gives devices to those who cannot pay.

service_area.note: Operates statewide in principle — "home-based ... services across North Carolina and virtually in Virginia and South Carolina" — but in-home coverage follows where an individual contract therapist lives. As of 2026-09-03 the therapists profiled on its own Providers page cover eastern Wake County, Cary/Apex/Holly Springs, Wake Forest and North Raleigh, the Triad (Guilford and Forsyth), Central NC and the Wilmington area. None is described as covering Charlotte or Mecklenburg. At the same time its own Hiring page advertises contract low vision OT posts in "Fayetteville, Wilmington, and Charlotte, North Carolina," which is direct evidence that Charlotte in-home coverage is being built rather than already staffed. Telehealth occupational therapy and counselling are offered anywhere in NC, so a Charlotte-area person can be served remotely today and possibly in person later. Ask which it will be before referring.

services.label: In-home low-vision occupational therapy
services.plain_language: A therapist comes to your home and works out how to keep doing everyday things with the sight you have.
services.notes: "Low Vision Rehab Solutions specializes in providing home-based" services "across North Carolina and virtually in Virginia and South Carolina." Clients are seen for roughly 2-hour visits over 6 to 8 sessions on average, varying with the level of vision loss and the goals set at the first visit. Common diagnoses named: macular degeneration, glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, other diseases of the retina and optic nerve, and neurological vision impairment.

services.label: Telehealth occupational therapy and counselling
services.plain_language: The same help by phone or video if nobody can come to your house.
services.notes: "Yes, telehealth is available for both occupational therapy and counseling services. We offer telehealth services in North Carolina, Virginia, and South Carolina." This is the route most likely to be available to a Charlotte-area person right now.

services.label: Counselling for the emotional adjustment to vision loss
services.plain_language: Someone to talk to about the grief and the loss of confidence, by phone or video.
services.notes: Offered as a distinct service and orderable on the physician referral form as a separate line from occupational therapy. Sessions are held by phone or video. The practice's FAQ describes the counsellors as licensed clinical social workers; the Providers page profiles a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counsellor and Qualified Supervisor. Counsellors, like the therapists, are independent contractors.

services.label: Assistive technology recommendation and training
services.plain_language: Advice on magnifiers, lighting and gadgets, and training to actually use them.
services.notes: The therapist recommends low vision devices and task and environment modifications as part of the goal-setting.

services.notes: Split into its own record on 2026-09-03. It is a separate 501(c)(3) with its own board, website and email (admin@lvrsfoundation.org, https://lvrsfoundation.org/), and its device mission covers all of North Carolina with no physician referral and no insurance gate — so a Charlotte-area person can use it whether or not a therapist covers their town. See lvrs-foundation for how to approach it and for the warning that no recipient application route is published.

name: Charlotte Area Transit System Special Transportation Service
one_line: Door-side van rides for people who cannot use regular CATS buses because of a disability, including vision loss.

service_area.note: ADA paratransit is mandated only within "the area up to 3/4 of a mile on either side of an existing fixed or local bus route," and runs only on the days and hours that the matching fixed route runs. Eligibility therefore depends on where the person lives relative to a bus route, not on which county they are in. An expanded STS+ service launched in Mint Hill in October 2024 beyond the mandated ADA area. Someone in Union, Cabarrus, Gaston or Iredell County is almost certainly outside it.

services.label: Shared-ride van service (ADA paratransit)
services.plain_language: A shared van for people who cannot ride the regular bus on their own because of a disability, including vision loss.

services.label: Curb-to-curb transportation within the ADA area
services.plain_language: Pick-up and drop-off at the curb, anywhere within 3/4 mile of a CATS bus route.

documentation_required: ADA paratransit eligibility application describing the disability, verified and signed by a medical/rehabilitation/healthcare professional
Possible in-person interview and functional assessment
cost: Certification is free. Once certified, STS fares are $3.50 one-way; a book of ten STS yellow tickets is $35.00; an STS monthly pass with unlimited rides is $140.00. Drivers cannot accept cash — the rider must have a yellow ticket or a monthly pass before boarding. STS certification also qualifies the person for the half-price ADA-Disabled fixed-route fare ($1.10 one-way, $44.00 monthly) when they can use a regular bus or the Blue Line, on presentation of a valid Medicare card or CATS Transit ID.
typical_wait: "After your interview and assessment are complete, STS will notify you of your eligibility within 21 days after we receive your completed application." The interview/assessment itself is scheduled by STS after the application arrives; how long that scheduling takes is not published.

access_path.action: Call STS on 1-833-656-7699 and ask for an ADA paratransit eligibility application
access_path.detail: Applications are issued by mail, by fax, or online. TTY 704-336-5051. Eleven trustees: ten appointed by the Mecklenburg Board of County Commissioners and one by the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Board of Education, four-year terms, county residents. name: VA Blind Rehabilitation Service (BRS) Continuum of Care
also_known_as: VA blind and low vision rehabilitation system
one_line: The VA's umbrella of vision-loss services for enrolled veterans: case management, home training, clinics, inpatient rehab, and devices.

service_area.note: Charlotte-area veterans are served by the Salisbury VA Health Care System (VISN 6), with VA-operated sites inside Mecklenburg County: the South Charlotte VA Clinic (3506 West Tyvola Rd) and the North Charlotte VA Clinic (8601 University East Dr), both of which VA lists under VA Salisbury health care. Verdict in_area confirmed. The 21-county Central Piedmont catchment is not enumerated on any VA-published page found. Some tiers of the continuum sit outside NC: the inpatient Blind Rehabilitation Center (see va-blind-rehabilitation-center-augusta), the VISN 6 VISOR program in Richmond, VA (see va-visor), and VICTORS, which VA publishes only in Northport, NY and Palo Alto, CA (see va-victors).

services.label: BROS in-home training

services.notes: See va-bros.

services.plain_language: Eye exams and training on magnifiers, lighting, and electronic devices to make the most of remaining sight.
services.notes: See va-low-vision-clinics and va-advanced-low-vision-clinic-salisbury.

services.label: VICTORS / VISOR outpatient programs

services.notes: See va-victors and va-visor.

services.plain_language: A live-in program lasting several weeks to relearn daily living from the ground up.
services.notes: See va-blind-rehabilitation-center-augusta. NC veterans are routed out of VISN 6.

services.label: Prosthetics & Sensory Aids (PSAS) assistive technology
services.plain_language: Free devices — electronic magnifiers, screen readers, talking devices, GPS aids — when prescribed by a VA clinician.
services.notes: See va-prosthetics-sensory-aids.

who_qualifies: Eligible for VA health benefits (or an active-duty service member) AND has a visual impairment, or has a designation of excess disability (impact on functional abilities) — VA's published three-part BRS eligibility test

Service connection is NOT required — blind rehabilitation is a health-care benefit, not a disability benefit. VA's Blind and Visual Impairment Rehabilitation Services page states the criteria as VA health benefit eligibility plus visual impairment, with no mention of service connection
A veteran can get blind rehab with zero service-connected rating, and can be denied compensation yet still be enrolled for health care
The true gate is VA health-care enrollment (VA Form 10-10EZ), which turns on character of discharge, not on a disability rating

Refer to a VIST Coordinator on any of VA's published triggers: trouble driving, bumping into things more often, an increase in falls that may relate to vision, trouble reading, trouble seeing items clearly, or any reported concern about visual functioning
documentation_required: VA health-care enrollment (VA Form 10-10EZ)
Eye report/exam documenting the visual impairment (acuity, visual field)
Program-specific documentation varies by entry point — see each child record
cost: Free to eligible enrolled veterans. Vision care and rehab are free to enrolled veterans; devices provided at no cost.
typical_wait: Not published — verification call required. The report states wait times are not published for any VA vision program it covers.

services.label: Prescription eyeglasses — narrower eligibility than the rest of vision care
services.plain_language: Glasses are NOT provided to every enrolled veteran. VA covers routine eye exams for everyone with VA health care, but eyeglasses only for veterans who meet specific criteria.
services.notes: VA publishes the eyeglasses criteria as: a compensable service-connected disability; former prisoner of war; Purple Heart recipient; receiving Title 38 U.S.C. 1151 benefits; or receiving an increased pension for being permanently housebound and in need of regular aid and attendance. This is the one place in the VA vision pathway where service connection genuinely matters — it does NOT apply to blind rehabilitation itself.

name: American Council of the Blind — ACB Community
one_line: Free daily community calls and hundreds of monthly virtual events by phone or Zoom for blind and low-vision people.

service_area.note: Nationwide/virtual (Zoom + phone dial-in). Usable from Charlotte with a phone.

services.label: Hundreds of virtual events monthly (peer support, hobbies, tech, health)
services.plain_language: Online and phone events every month on support, hobbies, technology, and health.
services.notes: Schedule at https://www.acb.org/acb-community-events

services.label: Daily community calls by phone or Zoom
services.plain_language: Join a group call any day of the week from your phone.

services.label: Podcasts and internet radio (ACB Media)
services.plain_language: Listen to ACB's podcasts and internet radio.

who_qualifies: Anyone. "ACB Community events are open to everyone. Membership in ACB is not required."
No diagnosis, eye report, referral, age limit or income test
cost: Free
typical_wait: Same day. Calls run every day and a person can join the first one after they get the joining details.

access_path.action: Get the joining details — this is the step people miss
access_path.detail: The Zoom link, meeting ID and password are deliberately NOT published on the events page: "link, meeting ID, and password for each meeting will not be available on this page." The phone route needs no email address, no computer and no sighted help, which makes this one of the very few services in this database a person can start entirely alone.

branches.condition: The person has no email address and cannot use one
branches.note: Use the telephone route only: 800-424-8666, press 1024. Everything works by phone; Zoom is optional.

access_path.action: Dial into a call from any telephone, or join by Zoom
access_path.detail: Every ACB Community event can be joined by telephone as well as by Zoom, so no computer, tablet or internet connection is needed. Hundreds of events run each month covering peer support, hobbies, technology and health.
requires: The day's joining details from the email list or the phone line

access_path.detail: community@acb.org is the published contact for questions about ACB Community: "For questions, please email community@acb.org."

access_path.action: For a person who also wants structured one-to-one support, pair this with Hadley
access_path.detail: ACB Community gives daily company from day one. Hadley adds a matched peer and an eight-week adjustment group. Together they cover the gap while a person waits months for rehabilitation services.

branches.condition: The person wants one-to-one peer support or structured coping sessions
branches.note: Free, also usable by telephone, also with no eye report required.

branches.condition: The person wants a local in-person group in the Charlotte area

contacts.general_email: community@acb.org (questions); ACB-Community-Events+subscribe@acblists.org (subscribe to the daily events list)

name: NC Lions Camp Dogwood
also_known_as: NC Lions Camp Dogwood for the Blind and Visually Impaired
is_program_of: North Carolina Lions Foundation
one_line: Week-long overnight summer camp sessions on Lake Norman for blind and visually impaired North Carolina adults.

service_area.note: All NC residents who are blind/VI. Located in Sherrills Ford, NC, on Lake Norman (report: within greater Charlotte / Catawba–Iredell). Limited out-of-state.

services.label: Week-long overnight summer sessions
services.plain_language: A week at camp with boating, fishing, swimming, adaptive water sports, archery, and arts and crafts.
services.notes: 2026 sessions run Session 1 (May 24–28) through Session 7 (July 12–16); some (e.g., Session 4, June 21–25) already showing a waiting list.

services.label: Social community with other blind/VI adults
services.plain_language: Spend the week with other adults who are blind or have low vision.
services.notes: Staff-supported; sighted companions welcome.

who_qualifies: "any resident of North Carolina" who is blind or visually impaired, meaning "a vision of 20/70 with the best correction" or worse
Aged "between the ages of 18-100+ years"

"All campers must be able to provide their own self-care skills, such as eating, bathing, dressing, and toileting." "If a camper needs assistance with these skills they are required to bring a caregiver with them."
"Sighted individuals may accompany the camper as a caregiver, companion, spouse, or minor child."
"Blind & visually impaired youth accompanied by a parent/guardian are welcome."
"Out of state campers may be accepted if space is available. Special pricing and conditions apply."
documentation_required: Camp Application Section 1 and Section 2, both downloadable from https://nclf.org/program-forms/
The camper's vision level, meeting the 20/70 best-corrected threshold
A caregiver named on the application if the camper needs help with eating, bathing, dressing or toileting
A $50 deposit to hold the place
cost: CONFLICT RESOLVED as of 2026-09-03. The camp's own Application, Fees & Schedule page gives $250.00 per week for a blind or visually impaired North Carolina resident, $300 for a caregiver and $500 for a companion, with a $50 deposit to hold a place. The older $225/$275/$400 figures are superseded. Transportation is $60 for the round trip between the station and camp, and does not include the bus or train ticket itself. Out-of-state campers pay special pricing. If the fee is a problem the camp's own instruction is: "If the fee poses a challenge, please reach out to your local Lions Club to explore sponsorship options."
typical_wait: SEASONAL, and currently between seasons. As of 2026-09-03 the camp's own page says "2027 Summer Schedule will be published soon" and the final payment deadline is listed as TBD, so there are no dates to apply for yet. The 2026 season ran seven weekly sessions from late May to mid-July and some filled with waiting lists. Anyone referred now is being referred to next summer, not to something that can help this month.

access_path.action: Check whether the next summer's schedule has been published before doing anything else
access_path.detail: https://nclionscampdogwood.org/application-fees-schedule/. As of 2026-09-03 it reads "2027 Summer Schedule will be published soon." Call (828) 478-2135 ext. 230 or email campdogwood@nclf.org to ask when dates open, and be clear with the person that this is a next-summer plan, not immediate help.

branches.condition: The person needs support now rather than next summer
branches.note: ACB Community runs daily calls a person can join the same day, and hadley offers peer matching and support groups with no waiting list. Camp Dogwood is worth applying for in parallel, not instead.

access_path.action: Check the eligibility gate honestly before applying: 20/70 or worse, aged 18 or over, and able to manage own self-care
access_path.detail: "All campers must be able to provide their own self-care skills, such as eating, bathing, dressing, and toileting." Someone who cannot must bring a caregiver at $300, which more than doubles the cost. A blind or visually impaired young person under 18 may attend accompanied by a parent or guardian.
requires: Age 18 or over, or a parent/guardian accompanying a younger camper
Independent self-care, or a named caregiver

access_path.action: If the fee is a barrier, approach a local Lions club for sponsorship BEFORE submitting the application
access_path.detail: The camp's published instruction is to "reach out to your local Lions Club to explore sponsorship options." There is also a Support a Camper form at https://nclf.org/public_files/SupportaCamper.pdf. County social workers and Lions clubs routinely help with this application. Sorting the money first avoids a deposit the person cannot pay.

branches.condition: No local Lions club contact is known
branches.note: Call the Foundation on (828) 478-2135 ext. 223 or (800) 662-7401 ext. 223 and ask which club covers the person's town.

access_path.action: Complete Camp Application Section 1 and Section 2 and return them with the $50 deposit
access_path.detail: Both sections are downloadable from https://nclf.org/program-forms/. Applications may also be requested by calling (828) 478-2135 ext. 230 or emailing campdogwood@nclf.org. Completed applications go to PO Box 39, Sherrills Ford, NC 28673. Note the forms are Word documents in two parts — someone who cannot read print will need help completing them.

access_path.action: Arrange travel, and add the $60 transport fee if arriving by train or bus
access_path.detail: The $60 covers the round trip between the station and camp and does not include the bus or train ticket. Camp is at 7062 Camp Dogwood Dr., Sherrills Ford, NC 28673, on Lake Norman — roughly 40 miles north of uptown Charlotte and not reachable by any Charlotte public transport, so this has to be planned.

access_path.action: Camp confirms a session place or puts the camper on a session waiting list
access_path.detail: Sessions filled and generated waiting lists in 2026. Final payment deadline for 2027 is published as TBD.

contacts.address: Camp: 7062 Camp Dogwood Dr., Sherrills Ford, NC 28673. Applications by post: PO Box 39, Sherrills Ford, NC 28673.

name: Out of Sight
one_line: Free volunteer-run virtual community for blind people — games, book clubs and conversation, joined through TeamTalk software.

service_area.note: National, virtual. Usable from Charlotte with internet access.

services.label: Virtual chat rooms incl. book clubs, games, adaptive cooking
services.plain_language: Online rooms where you can join a book club, play games, or talk about cooking without sight.

who_qualifies: Anyone; no eligibility test, diagnosis or documentation is published
The site is built for blind and low vision users and is run by blind volunteers
cost: Free. "There is no cost to join! Likewise, there is no charge to participate in any event or program."
typical_wait: Same day in principle, but only after the membership application is approved and the TeamTalk software is installed and working. Approval turnaround is not published.

access_path.action: Understand the real barrier before recommending this: it needs a computer or smartphone and a separate piece of software
access_path.detail: Out of Sight runs on TeamTalk, described by the site as "a very accessible chat client," "free to download and easy to use," available for "Windows, Mac, iPhone, or Android." A microphone or headset is also required. There is no telephone dial-in. That makes this a poor fit for someone with no computer or no confidence installing software, and a good fit for someone who already uses a screen reader. If in doubt, offer acb-community instead, which works from any telephone.

branches.condition: The person has no computer or smartphone, or cannot install software
branches.note: ACB Community runs everything by ordinary telephone with no software at all. hadley also works by phone.

branches.condition: The person needs help getting a device or learning to use it first
branches.note: The NC Assistive Technology Program demonstrates and loans devices; nc-dsb-independent-living teaches the skills to use them.

access_path.action: Apply for free membership
access_path.detail: The application asks for "your first and last name, your email address, and a nickname/screen name." The registration link on the site is https://out-of-sight.net/wp-login.php?action=register. An email address is therefore required. Installation guides are published for Windows, iDevice and Android at https://out-of-sight.net/access-using-an-idevice and https://out-of-sight.net/access-using-an-android-device.

access_path.action: Install TeamTalk and join a room from the weekly schedule
access_path.detail: Weekly schedule at https://out-of-sight.net/weekly-schedule-of-events, event descriptions at https://out-of-sight.net/description-of-site-events, game rules at https://out-of-sight.net/game-rules, and TeamTalk keyboard shortcuts at https://out-of-sight.net/teamtalk-shortcuts. Note that the Windows installer is served from a Dropbox link rather than from the TeamTalk publisher's own site, which some people and some workplace or library computers will refuse — worth knowing before sitting down with someone to set it up.

access_path.action: If something goes wrong, email the volunteers
access_path.detail: General enquiries and complaints: OOSNHQ@gmail.com. Website problems: modem7373@gmail.com. Events and presentations: Karen Santiago, KarenxSantiago@msn.com. There are also two email discussion lists a member can subscribe to, described on https://out-of-sight.net/connect-with-us.

confidence_note: Verified 2026-09-03. https://out-of-sight.net returns HTTP 200 and is currently active — it carries a Fall Auction 2026 page. It is "managed by a Board of Trustees consisting of five members" who are volunteers, so it is a small volunteer community rather than a service organisation, and its published contacts are personal Gmail and MSN addresses. Confidence stays medium not because anything is doubtful but because there is no organisation behind it to hold to a standard: no phone, no office, no staff, no published response time.
open_questions: Email OOSNHQ@gmail.com and ask: how long does membership approval take, and is a person told when they are approved?
Email OOSNHQ@gmail.com and ask: will a volunteer help a new member install TeamTalk over the phone, or is the person on their own with the written guides?
Email OOSNHQ@gmail.com and ask: can an agency such as Lions Services refer someone, or must the person apply themselves? The site publishes no referral route.
Ask whether any event is suitable for someone who is deaf-blind, given that everything is voice-based over TeamTalk.

name: Disability Rights & Resources
also_known_as: Gaston County Advocacy Council for People with Disabilities (hosted)
one_line: Charlotte Center for Independent Living: advocacy, independent living skills, travel training, peer mentoring and audio description.

service_area.note: GEOGRAPHY VERDICT CONFIRMED 2026-09-03 from the organization's own site: a four-county service area of Mecklenburg, Gaston, Union and Cabarrus in North Carolina's southern piedmont. All four are on the working county list in docs/geography-definition.md, so in_area is correct. Does not cover Iredell, Lincoln, Rowan, Cleveland, Stanly or Catawba, nor York or Lancaster in SC.

services.label: Advocacy and ADA technical assistance
services.plain_language: Help standing up for your rights, getting barriers removed, and understanding what the disability laws entitle you to.
services.notes: Includes community forums. Department contact: martymusser@disability-rights.org

services.label: Independent living skills training
services.plain_language: Learning practical skills to live on your own — budgeting, getting around, filling in job applications.

services.label: Let's All Go! travel training
services.plain_language: One-to-one training on how to use the buses, light rail and streetcar so you can get around without driving.
services.notes: Directly useful to someone who has stopped driving because of sight loss. Department contact: jordanhayes@disability-rights.org

services.label: Peer mentoring
services.plain_language: Being paired with another person with a disability who has been through it and can help you set goals.
services.notes: Cross-disability, not vision-specific. Whether DRR can pair a newly blind person with a blind peer mentor is still unverified — see open_questions.

services.label: Audio description
services.plain_language: Spoken descriptions of things you cannot see — visual media and public art.
services.notes: This is DRR's one explicitly vision-related service on its own published services list.

services.label: My Home, My Choice community integration
services.plain_language: Help moving out of an institution and into your own home.
services.notes: Published requirements: income, a commitment to change, and the ability to live safely and independently.

services.label: Powerful Youth With Disabilities (ages 14-24)
services.plain_language: Goal-setting and leadership for young people with disabilities aged 14 to 24.
services.notes: Department contact: cherinebentley@disability-rights.org

services.label: Information and referral, and emergency/disaster preparedness resources
services.plain_language: Being pointed to other services, and help planning for an emergency when you have a disability.

who_qualifies: People with disabilities living in Mecklenburg, Gaston, Union or Cabarrus counties
Powerful Youth With Disabilities: ages 14-24
My Home, My Choice: requires income, a commitment to change, and the ability to live safely and independently
No vision-specific eligibility gate is published — this is a cross-disability Center for Independent Living, not a blindness agency
documentation_required: Not published — verification call required
cost: Not published — verification call required. Centers for Independent Living are typically free to consumers, but DRR does not publish this and it must not be assumed.
typical_wait: Not published — verification call required

access_path.action: Call 704-537-0550, or email mailto@disability-rights.org, or use the contact form at https://disability-rights.org/contact/
access_path.detail: Office hours published as Monday-Thursday 9:00am-5:00pm. The office is by appointment only — do not send anyone to drop in.

branches.condition: Person lives outside Mecklenburg, Gaston, Union or Cabarrus county
branches.note: DRR's published service area is those four counties only. Other NC counties are served by different Centers for Independent Living — ask DRR which one covers the person's county.

branches.condition: Person is a veteran
branches.note: Ask about military service first. VA blind rehabilitation is more comprehensive and has no comparable waitlist; DRR's travel training and advocacy can run alongside it.

access_path.action: Say which programme you want, because DRR routes by department
access_path.detail: Advocacy: martymusser@disability-rights.org. Let's All Go! travel training: jordanhayes@disability-rights.org. Youth services ages 14-24: cherinebentley@disability-rights.org. General: mailto@disability-rights.org.

access_path.action: Ask specifically whether the peer mentor can be someone who is blind or has low vision
access_path.detail: DRR's peer mentoring is cross-disability. A person newly losing their sight usually wants a blind peer, and DRR does not publish whether it can provide one.

branches.condition: Person specifically wants blind or low-vision peer support
branches.note: The NFB Mecklenburg County chapter and Metrolina Association for the Blind's peer groups are the vision-specific alternatives.

access_path.action: Pair DRR with a blindness-specific service — DRR is cross-disability and does not do vision rehabilitation
access_path.detail: DRR's published services include no low vision exams, no orientation and mobility instruction and no assistive technology programme. Its travel training and audio description are genuinely useful alongside vision rehabilitation, not instead of it.

branches.condition: Person needs vision rehabilitation or independent living skills for sight loss
branches.note: NC DSB Independent Living, or Metrolina Association for the Blind, are the vision-specific routes.

name: United States Association of Blind Athletes (USABA)
one_line: National membership body for blind and low-vision athletes — join online from Charlotte; local play means finding or travelling to a club.

service_area.note: GEOGRAPHY VERDICT CHANGED from statewide_travel_required to partial. USABA is a national body in Colorado Springs, not an NC statewide body, so the statewide rule in docs/geography-definition.md does not apply to it. Membership, the classification information and the sport pages are fully usable from Charlotte online with no travel — that part is in_area in substance. But USABA publishes no North Carolina member club, and its Blind Soccer Development Program currently lists sites in Maryland, Texas, Los Angeles and Miami, not Charlotte. Actually playing a sport therefore requires either travel or building something local. 'partial' captures both halves honestly; statewide_travel_required overstated the travel barrier for joining and understated it for competing.

services.label: National membership and sport programmes
services.plain_language: Join online, then get connected to blind sport across the country.
services.notes: Sports listed on the site: goalball, blind soccer, track and field, beep baseball, triathlon, cycling, judo, winter sports, powerlifting, swimming. Membership runs through the Sport:80 platform reached from https://www.usaba.org/join/.

services.label: Help finding a goalball programme near you
services.plain_language: Email USABA's goalball coordinator and ask what is nearest to Charlotte.
services.notes: USABA's goalball page names Linda Welborn, lwelborn@usaba.org, as the person to contact to locate a programme. No North Carolina club is listed on the site.

services.label: Visual classification information

name: North Carolina Lions Foundation
one_line: Statewide Lions charity: free white canes and loaned magnifiers for any blind North Carolinian, Camp Dogwood, screenings and grants.

service_area.note: Statewide NC (local clubs across the Charlotte area).

services.label: Free mobility canes
services.plain_language: A free white cane, posted to you, no charge and no income test.
services.notes: "available free of charge to any blind or visually impaired person in North Carolina." Request form at https://nclf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Cane-Order-Form-PDF.pdf, emailed to canes@nclf.org. This is the fastest, lowest-barrier thing in this record and it was missing entirely.

services.label: Low vision aids on free long-term loan
services.plain_language: A borrowed magnifier, free, for as long as you need it.
services.notes: Used magnification devices are "loaned for as long as needed, free of charge." No published application form — ask the Foundation office on (828) 478-2135 ext. 223.

services.label: Camp Dogwood
services.plain_language: A week-long summer camp on Lake Norman for adults who are blind or have low vision.
services.notes: The Foundation runs it: "provides an exciting summer camp experience for over 800 blind and visually impaired campers each year." See the camp-dogwood record for eligibility, fees and dates.

services.label: VSP vision care voucher programme — CURRENTLY PAUSED
services.plain_language: Vouchers for a free eye exam and glasses through a local Lions club — not being issued at the moment.
services.notes: The Foundation's Program Forms page carries a VSP Voucher Information Form in English and Spanish, marked "Program currently paused," requiring the applicant to "contact a Local Lions Club for assistance," returned by post, fax or email to VSP@nclf.org. This is the North Carolina Lions channel into VSP Eyes of Hope, and it is paused for the same reason VSP has paused national distribution — see the vsp-eyes-of-hope record. Do not promise a voucher; ask whether the pause has lifted.

services.label: Free vision screenings — KidSight and the Mobile Screening Unit
services.plain_language: A quick vision check at an event. This is NOT a full eye exam and does NOT produce the eye report a rehabilitation agency needs.
services.notes: Screening calendar at https://nclf.org/mobile-screening-unit-calendar/. Screenings are not diagnostic and will not satisfy Metrolina or DSB documentation requirements.

services.label: Education grants for sighted children of visually impaired parents
services.plain_language: Scholarship money for the sighted child of a parent who is blind or has low vision.
services.notes: Grant policy and application at https://nclf.org/program-forms/ (EDPolicy.rev-2025.pdf and NCLFED.rev2025.pdf, both dated 2025). A distinctive benefit that exists almost nowhere else in this database.

services.label: Support for the annual Deaf Blind retreat and the VIP Fishing Tournament
services.plain_language: The Foundation helps pay for the yearly deaf-blind retreat and the fishing tournament for people with vision loss.
services.notes: "Annual support is provided to the Deaf Blind for their annual retreat." Relevant to the deaf-blind pathway, where options are scarce — ask the Foundation office who organises the retreat and how a person gets a place. See also nc-lions-vip-fishing-tournament.

services.label: Eyeglass recycling
services.plain_language: Somewhere to donate used spectacles.
services.notes: https://nclf.org/recycling-programs/. A donation route, not a service a person in need receives.

Camp Dogwood: NC residents with best-corrected vision of 20/70 or worse, aged 18-100+, able to manage self-care or bringing a caregiver
VSP vouchers: applicant must "contact a Local Lions Club for assistance" — the club, not the Foundation, initiates; programme currently paused

name: NC Medicaid — Vision (Routine Eye Examination and Visual Aids)
one_line: NC Medicaid covers a routine eye exam and glasses (every 2 years for adults, yearly under 21) plus medical eye exams for disease.

service_area.note: Statewide NC.

services.label: Covered routine eye exam and glasses
services.plain_language: If you have NC Medicaid, a routine eye exam and prescription glasses are covered — once every two years for adults 21 and older, every year under 21.
services.notes: No PCP referral is required for routine eye exams. Medicaid does NOT cover eye exams or glasses via telehealth.

services.label: Medical eye exams for disease
services.plain_language: Exams for eye diseases like glaucoma, cataracts, macular degeneration, and diabetic eye disease.
services.notes: A Medicaid-enrolled optometrist/ophthalmologist can produce the eye report rehab agencies need.

who_qualifies: NC Medicaid and NC Health Choice beneficiaries — routine eye exams and visual aids are covered for beneficiaries regardless of age

Adults 21 and older may get a routine eye exam and prescription glasses once every two years (NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 6B, amended May 1, 2024; the adult benefit has been in place since January 1, 2019)
Children and young people 20 and under: annually, under EPSDT (Clinical Coverage Policy 6A)
Someone who is not enrolled must apply for NC Medicaid first — see step 1 of the access path
documentation_required: Active (non-expired) Medicaid card
cost: Covered by Medicaid — no cost to the beneficiary for the covered exam and covered visual aids. Coverage includes select eyeglasses and medically necessary contact lenses.
typical_wait: Depends on provider

access_path.action: If not already enrolled, apply for NC Medicaid at epass.nc.gov, by phone on 1-888-245-0179, or in person at the county Department of Social Services
access_path.detail: In Mecklenburg County the DSS is Child, Family and Adult Services — walk-ins accepted, or call to schedule an in-person or phone interview. On the application NC Medicaid is called 'Medical Assistance'; an NCID account is needed to start online. How to apply: https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/apply. Skip this step if the person already has an active card.

branches.condition: The person has served in the US military
branches.note: Ask about military service first. VA eye care and blind rehabilitation are free to enrolled veterans and more comprehensive; a VSO can pursue VA enrolment alongside or instead of Medicaid.

branches.condition: The person is uninsured, low income, and not eligible for Medicaid
branches.note: Free exam by a volunteer optometrist, but a caseworker must submit the application and the person must be uninsured.

access_path.action: Find a Medicaid-enrolled optometrist or ophthalmologist
access_path.detail: Call NC Medicaid on 1-888-245-0179, or the NC Medicaid Beneficiary Ombudsman on 1-877-201-3750, and ask for an eye doctor taking new Medicaid patients. No PCP referral is required for a routine eye exam.

branches.condition: Person is in a managed care plan
branches.note: Check the practice takes that specific plan before booking — participation varies plan by plan, not just by 'Medicaid'.

branches.condition: Person wants Duke Eye Center and has Healthy Blue
branches.note: Duke Eye clinics do NOT participate in Healthy Blue; check plan participation before booking.

access_path.action: Book the exam in person — telehealth is not covered for eye exams or glasses
access_path.detail: Take the Medicaid card. If it is more than two years since the last covered adult exam, the exam and glasses should both be covered.

access_path.action: Ask for a written copy of the eye report before leaving
access_path.detail: The report naming the diagnosis and best-corrected acuity is the document Metrolina Association for the Blind, NC DSB and most other rehabilitation agencies in this dataset require. Getting it at the appointment saves weeks.

branches.condition: The exam shows significant permanent vision loss
branches.note: 980-296-6820. Take the eye report there — it is what DSB asks for at intake.

name: DSB Transition Services for High School Students
is_program_of: North Carolina Division of Services for the Blind
one_line: DSB help for students with vision loss, from as early as age 14, planning the move from school to work or college.

services.plain_language: A counselor who works with the student, the school and the family to plan what happens after graduation.
services.notes: NCDHHS: 'If you are a high school student who is blind, has a visual impairment, or if you have both vision and hearing loss, we can help you plan your move from school to employment.' Counselors can work with teachers and guidance counselors.

services.label: Career exploration from age 14
services.plain_language: Trying out the world of work early, to figure out what the student actually wants to do.
services.notes: NCDHHS: 'You can start your school-to-work transition as early as age 14 to explore the world of work and identify your career interests.'

services.label: Summer Transition Programs at the DSB Career and Training Center

services.notes: Held at the DSB Career and Training Center in Raleigh — an overnight trip from Charlotte.

services.label: College Prep program
services.plain_language: A programme for students planning to go on to college.

services.label: Help finding and paying for vocational or college training
services.plain_language: Help picking a school that matches the career goal, and finding money to pay for it.
services.notes: NCDHHS says financial resources may include assistance from the Division of Services for the Blind.

who_qualifies: High school students who are blind, have a visual impairment, or have both vision and hearing loss
Career exploration can begin as early as age 14

NC resident who meets the criteria for low vision or legal blindness, and whose vision impairment prevents them from finding or keeping a job — the same eligibility test as DSB Vocational Rehabilitation, because transition services are delivered inside VR
Whether a student must be enrolled in a public school, or have an IEP or 504 plan, is Not published — verification call required
documentation_required: A current eye report documenting the visual impairment, as for DSB Vocational Rehabilitation
VR application forms, which the counselor supplies and helps complete
Whether the school's IEP or 504 documentation is also required is Not published — verification call required
cost: Free
typical_wait: Not published — verification call required. access_path.action: Ask first whether the student is in a military family or has served
access_path.detail: Rarely relevant for a student, but a student veteran or a student eligible for VA care through their own service should be checked against VA blind rehabilitation, which is more comprehensive and has no comparable waitlist.

branches.condition: Student has served in the military

one_line: Several national guide dog schools take NC applicants; you apply yourself, and eligibility and cost differ school to school.

service_area.note: Verdict retained. Guiding Eyes accepts applicants anywhere in the United States and Canada; The Seeing Eye, Guide Dog Foundation and Dogs Inc are all out of state; Mira USA is NC-based at Southern Pines, roughly 100 miles from Charlotte, and serves children only. In-person training at the school campus is the norm, so travel is required whichever school is chosen.

services.label: Guide dog training and placement

who_qualifies: ELIGIBILITY DIFFERS MATERIALLY BY SCHOOL — do not treat these as interchangeable

Guiding Eyes for the Blind: legally blind (visual acuity 20/200 or less in the better-seeing eye with correction, or a visual field of 20 degrees or less); at least 16, no upper age limit; resident of the United States or Canada; walks outdoors regularly and independently using a white cane or guide dog; has completed Orientation and Mobility training; able to feed, exercise and care for a dog

The Seeing Eye: at least 16; 'a degree of vision which will not interfere in the safe and effective working relationship with a Seeing Eye dog'; independent travel skills adequate for working with a guide dog; an active daily routine giving the dog real travel destinations; assessed via personal references, agency referrals, a personal interview and a physician's report

Dogs Inc (formerly Southeastern Guide Dogs): guide dog programme from age 15, with a Guide Dogs for Teens programme for ages 15-19; Orientation and Mobility training must be completed before receiving a dog
Mira Foundation USA: blind CHILDREN aged 11 to 16 only — note this is 11-16 on Mira's own site, not 11-17
Common to all: the applicant applies personally. No school in this group takes a professional referral in place of an application.
documentation_required: Vision assessment form completed by an eye doctor, proving legal blindness
Medical form from a primary care physician — Guiding Eyes requires one dated within the last 6 months; The Seeing Eye requires a physician's report
Personal references
Signed Release of Information form
Background check authorisation (Guiding Eyes)
Evidence of completed Orientation and Mobility training
cost: MOSTLY free, but NOT universally — the Phase 1 'Free (schools listed)' was wrong. Guiding Eyes: no cost for the training programme; graduates should budget $80-$100 a month for dog food and supplies, with a $600 annual veterinary stipend provided. Dogs Inc: dogs and services at no cost, plus free premium dog food, annual veterinary care and flea and tick preventatives. Mira USA: free of charge. THE SEEING EYE CHARGES A FEE: $150 for a first placement and $50 for return students, covering the dog, equipment, transportation, room and board during training and lifetime follow-up — and $1 for veterans.
typical_wait: Varies by school. Dogs Inc publishes an average waiting period of 6 to 12 months from application to match. Guiding Eyes asks for the supporting documents within 3 months of applying so the wait time is not delayed. The Seeing Eye and Mira USA do not publish a wait.

documentation_required: For NC DeafBlind Project services the child must be registered on the NC DeafBlind Census — "Children with combined vision and hearing loss must be registered on the NC DeafBlind Census to receive DeafBlind Services."

Census eligibility is functional as well as documented: "Children with COMBINED FUNCTIONAL or documented vision and hearing loss which may interfere with their ability to a) communicate and interact with others in educational and/or social settings; to access information (spoken, social media, print); and b) move about safely and efficiently in familiar and unfamiliar environments" — so a child with no formal dual diagnosis may still count
The census registration form is a Qualtrics form: https://ncdpi.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4Z45fXzDUrDagmO
After census registration, the ECU/TSP Teacher Request Form starts teacher support services: https://ecu.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_7TY9q3ieIRjdLxj
No documentation at all is required for the ECAC parent centre side, which helps any family of a child with any disability birth to 26
cost: Free
typical_wait: Not published — verification call required for the family support side. The census itself is on a fixed federal cycle: "The count is a snapshot of eligible students on December 1st", so census timing is annual, and since 2024 the data collection runs through ECATS, the state education data system. A child registered after a December count may wait for the next cycle to appear in the federal count, although the project's family support does not obviously depend on that — ask.

access_path.action: Call the ECAC helpline on 1-800-962-6817 (or 704-892-1321 / 704-892-5028) or email ecac@ecacmail.org — no census registration needed for this
access_path.detail: "All of our services are provided at no cost to families!" ECAC is the NC Parent Training and Information Center and helps families of children with ANY disability from birth to 26, so a family can get a parent educator immediately without waiting for anything to be registered. Office: 907 Barra Row, Suite 103, Davidson, NC 28036 — inside the greater Charlotte area, about 20 miles north of uptown. Online request form: https://www.ecac-parentcenter.org/work-with-a-parent-educator/

branches.note: Run this in parallel. ELSSP-VI provides a licensed Teacher of the Visually Impaired in the home, free, and starts through the NC Infant Toddler Program.

branches.note: The district's Exceptional Children process runs the child's educational entitlement. ECAC exists partly to help parents navigate exactly that process.
